items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I received 25 dollars for that gig and the same for another I did with Peek-a-Boo in the city, which was not a stag party but a dance

ctx.x: But Jimmy was in with the rich folks downtown and he played many high society functions. The first one I did with him was a stag party for some business men who had rented a Hudson River cruising boat and invited about 400 men to cruise up the Hudson. We played but there was no dancing as there were no women to dance with. Finally we docked somewhere and everybody went ashore where a big picnic with all kinds of seafood and kegs of beer were waiting for everyone including the band. The committee of this outing…

I received 25 dollars for that gig and the same for another I did with Peek-a-Boo in the city, which was not a stag party but a dance and we had all the steaks and beer we could eat and drink. That was something that Peek-a-Boo always asked for his musicians and himself when he was having a gig.
Ralph Cooper, who was a dancer turned orchestra leader,
